note: Registre des formats d'examens. Pour suivre un changement officiel, on modifie ce fichier seulement : le moteur diisoo-exams2.js lit les tâches, les durées et les banques d'items ici. Les tests sont originaux (créés pour Diisoo), construits sur le format publié de chaque examen. Aucun sujet officiel n'est copié.

ielts.nom: IELTS Life Skills A1 · Speaking and Listening
ielts.confiance: Test de 16 à 18 minutes, à deux candidats avec un examinateur : partie 1 (poser et répondre à des questions sur des sujets familiers), partie 2 (écouter un enregistrement, répondre, puis discuter), d'après IDP et le British Council. La répartition du temps n'est pas publiée : les durées sont des durées d'entraînement. Diisoo adapte le test pour un candidat seul.
ielts.resume: Partie 1 : questions personnelles, sujets familiers, poser des questions. Partie 2 : écouter un enregistrement en prenant des notes, répondre, puis discuter : décrire, donner ses préférences et les justifier, développer.

taches.consigne: L'examinateur pose une question. Réponds par une phrase courte.
Réponds en une ou deux phrases simples.
Dans le test, tu poses aussi des questions. Pose 3 questions à l'examinateur sur le thème.
Écoute l'enregistrement en prenant des notes. Puis dis ce que tu as compris : qui parle, et ce qu'il ou elle fait.
Discute du thème de l'enregistrement. Donne ton avis.

p1b: What time do you get up?
What do you eat for breakfast?
How do you go to work or school?
What do you do in the evening?
ask: Ask the examiner three questions about his or her day. For example: What time do you get up?

p2a.t: Hello, my name is Anna. I live in London with my sister. Every morning I get up at seven o'clock. I have toast and tea for breakfast. Then I take the bus to work. I work in a shop near the station. In the evening I cook dinner and watch television.

p2b: Do you get up early or late?
What do you like to eat in the morning?
How do people travel to work in your town?

p1b: Do you live in a house or a flat?
How many rooms are there in your home?
ask: Ask the examiner three questions about his or her home. For example: How many rooms do you have?

p2a.t: My name is David. I live in a small flat with my brother. We have a kitchen, two bedrooms and a balcony. Our neighbours are friendly. On Saturdays we clean the flat and then we go to the market to buy fruit and vegetables.

p2b: What can you buy at a market?
Is it good to have friendly neighbours? Why?

p1b: Do you go shopping every week?
What do you buy at the shop?
Do you drink a lot of water?
What do you do when you are ill?
ask: Ask the examiner three questions about shopping. For example: Where do you buy your food?

p2a.t: Hello, this is Maria. Yesterday I went to the shop because I needed some medicine for my cough. The shop was open until eight o'clock. I bought medicine, water and some oranges. It cost eleven pounds. Today I feel better, and I am going to walk in the park.

p2b: Is it important to drink water? Why?
Where do you buy medicine in your town?
Do you like walking in the park?

enregistrements.neighbours: My name is Karim. I live in a house in Thiès. My neighbours are very kind. Every morning the old man next door says hello and gives me fresh bread. On Sundays we all eat lunch together in the street.
enregistrements.family: Hello, I am Fatou. I have a big family. I live with my mother, my father and three brothers. My grandmother is seventy years old. On Sundays we visit her and we eat rice and fish together.
enregistrements.free-time: My name is Peter. In my free time I like football. I play with my friends on Saturday afternoon. After the game we drink tea and talk. On Sunday I listen to music and read a book at home.
enregistrements.work: Hello, my name is Sara. I work in a hospital. I start work at eight o'clock and I finish at four o'clock. I help sick people every day. I like my job because my colleagues are very friendly.
enregistrements.shopping: I am John. Today I am at the market. I need rice, tomatoes and onions. The rice costs six hundred francs. The woman is nice and gives me a small gift. Then I pay and go home with my bags.
enregistrements.travel: My name is Aminata. Next week I travel to Dakar by bus. The journey takes two hours. I take one small bag, my phone and some water. My cousin waits for me at the station. We will visit the sea together.
enregistrements.health: Hello, this is Tom. Yesterday I had a headache and a fever. I went to the doctor in the morning. He gave me some medicine and said, drink a lot of water and rest. Today I feel much better.
enregistrements.food: My name is Awa. My favourite food is chicken with rice. My mother cooks it on Fridays. We also eat fruit and drink fresh juice. I do not like very spicy food, but my brother loves it.
enregistrements.shopping_food: I am Lisa. Every Saturday I buy food at the supermarket. This week I buy bread, milk, eggs and apples. The total is twelve pounds. I use my card to pay and put everything in a bag.
enregistrements.transport_travel: Hello, I am Ibrahima. I go to work by bus. The bus stop is near my house. The bus comes at seven fifteen and the ticket costs two hundred francs. Sometimes the road is busy and I arrive late.
enregistrements.health_emergencies: This is Emma. Last night my neighbour fell in the kitchen and hurt her arm. I called the ambulance and the number is nine nine nine. The ambulance arrived in ten minutes and took her to hospital.
enregistrements.family_reunion: My name is Moussa. I live in London and my wife and two children live in Senegal. I miss them every day. I phone them on Sunday evening. I hope they come to London next year and live with me.
enregistrements.airport: Hello, I am Daniel. I am at the airport. My flight to Paris leaves at ten thirty. I show my passport and my ticket at the desk. I give one big bag to the woman. Then I wait at gate number five.
enregistrements.hotel: My name is Julie. I have a room at the hotel for three nights. The room has a bed, a shower and a television. Breakfast is at seven in the restaurant. The hotel is quiet and clean, and the staff are polite.
enregistrements.money: I am Ousmane. I have fifty pounds in my wallet. I buy a book for ten pounds and a shirt for twenty pounds. The shop assistant gives me my change. I put the rest of the money in my bag.
enregistrements.clothes: My name is Rose. Today it is cold, so I wear a warm jacket and long trousers. My brother wears a blue shirt and black shoes. On Fridays many people in my town wear traditional clothes.
enregistrements.friends: Hello, I am Cheikh. I have a good friend called Paul. We study together and we play football on Saturdays. He is funny and always helps me. Next weekend we go to the cinema with two other friends.
enregistrements.phone: My name is Lucy. I have a new phone. I use it to call my family and to send messages. I also take photos and look for information on the internet. I charge my phone every night.
enregistrements.jobs: Hello, I am Mamadou. My father is a farmer and my mother is a teacher. My sister is a nurse and my brother is a driver. I want to be a mechanic. I like cars and I like to repair things.
enregistrements.restaurant: I am Nina. Tonight I am in a restaurant with my family. The waiter brings the menu. I order grilled fish and a salad. My father orders chicken. The food is hot and delicious, and we pay at the end.
enregistrements.weekend: My name is Ali. This weekend I am very busy. On Saturday morning I clean my room and wash my clothes. In the afternoon I visit my uncle. On Sunday I go to the beach with my friends and we play volleyball.
enregistrements.festivals: Hello, I am Khady. My favourite festival is Tabaski. Before the festival we buy new clothes. On the day we pray, then we eat meat with our family and give food to poor people. It is a happy day.
enregistrements.farming: I am Samba. I live in a village and I am a farmer. I grow millet and peanuts. I also have two cows and ten chickens. In the morning I give water to the animals. The rainy season is very important for my work.
enregistrements.bank: My name is Grace. I go to the bank on Monday morning. I want to open an account, so I show my passport and fill in a form. Then I go to the post office to send a letter to my mother.
enregistrements.school: Hello, I am Fatima. I study English at school three times a week. My teacher is kind and gives us homework. I practice new words every day. After school I read in the library and I ask questions.
enregistrements.home: I am Mark. I live in a small flat on the second floor. There is one bedroom, a kitchen and a bathroom. The flat is warm and bright. I pay rent every month, and the landlord is a friendly man.
enregistrements.holidays: My name is Mariama. I love the rainy season, but for holidays I prefer the sunny weather. Last summer I stayed at my aunt's house near the sea. It was hot, so we swam every afternoon and ate ice cream.

retell.t: Good morning. Today I want to talk about how plants grow. Plants need three things: water, light and air. Farmers in Senegal often plant seeds just before the rainy season because the soil is wet and the sun is strong. When a plant does not get enough water, its leaves turn yellow, and it grows more slowly. Some farmers use drip irrigation to give each plant exactly the water it needs.

Many universities now offer online courses. Students can watch lectures at any time and study at their own speed. This is useful for people who work during the day. However, online learning also has a problem: some students feel alone and lose motivation. For this reason, many courses include group chats and weekly video meetings with the teacher.

Many young entrepreneurs start small businesses with limited money. By saving carefully, learning from customers, and using social media to advertise, they can build successful companies that create jobs in their communities.

Sleep is essential for learning. During the night, the brain organizes new information and stores it in memory, which is why students who sleep well usually perform better on tests than those who stay awake studying.

Tourism is a major source of income for many countries. Visitors spend money on hotels, restaurants, transport, and souvenirs, and this spending supports thousands of families who work in the tourism industry.

retell.t: Good afternoon. Today we will look at how cities manage waste. Every day, a large city produces thousands of tons of garbage. Some cities separate plastic, paper and food waste so that it can be recycled or turned into compost. This reduces pollution and also creates jobs. However, recycling only works when residents take part, so education campaigns are very important.

Let me explain why people feel tired in the afternoon. After lunch, the body uses a lot of energy to digest food, and blood sugar can drop. At the same time, our natural body clock creates a small dip in alertness. A short walk, a glass of water, or a ten-minute rest can help people feel more awake and focused.

readaloud: A balanced diet includes fruit, vegetables, protein, and whole grains. Doctors advise people to drink enough water, reduce sugar, and eat at regular times so that the body receives the energy it needs throughout the day.

Deforestation is the permanent removal of trees from large areas. It destroys the homes of many animals, increases carbon in the air, and often leads to soil erosion, which makes farming more difficult for local communities.

Mobile banking has changed how many Africans manage their money. With a simple phone, people can send payments, save small amounts, and pay bills without traveling to a bank, which saves both time and transport costs.

Scientists believe that learning a second language improves memory and concentration. Students who speak two languages often switch between tasks more easily and may keep their minds active longer as they grow older.

retell.t: Good morning. Today I would like to talk about mobile money. Mobile money lets people send and receive money using only a phone number. It is especially useful in rural areas where banks are far away. Small traders can accept payments easily, and families can send support to relatives in minutes. However, users must protect their secret code to avoid fraud.

Let us consider why bees are important. Bees carry pollen from flower to flower, which helps plants produce fruit and seeds. Without bees, many crops such as mangoes and cashew nuts would produce much less. Unfortunately, pesticides and the loss of natural habitats are reducing bee populations. Farmers can help by planting flowers and using fewer chemicals.

readaloud: International trade allows countries to exchange goods and services that they cannot produce cheaply on their own. Port cities benefit greatly, because ships, warehouses, and transport companies create thousands of jobs for local workers.

Public libraries were originally built to give ordinary citizens access to knowledge. Today they also offer digital resources, children's programs, and quiet spaces where people can prepare for exams or search for employment.

Renewable energy comes from sources that do not run out, such as the sun and the wind. Although installing solar panels can be expensive at first, families usually save money in the long term because sunlight is free.

Effective time management is an essential skill for students and workers alike. By making a daily list, setting priorities, and avoiding distractions, people can complete more tasks and feel less stress at the end of the day.

retell.t: Welcome to today's lecture on teamwork. In a good team, each person has a clear role and everyone listens to the others. Meetings should be short and focused, and tasks must have deadlines. When conflicts appear, team members should talk calmly and look for a solution together. Teams that communicate well finish their projects faster and with better results.

Today we will discuss how markets set prices. When many people want a product but there is only a small quantity, the price goes up. When there is too much of a product and few buyers, the price goes down. Farmers know this well, because the price of tomatoes drops during harvest season when the market is full.
